body:
OWNER FOLLOW-UP AUDIT — the live `/scala/getting-started/` page is better but still extremely thin, exactly as the owner says.

Measured against the current uncommitted scout delta at HEAD `39c745d` and the live server:

- The page demonstrates only `StorySource -> SurfaceAnalyzer -> SpanSet`: text normalization, sentences, tokens, offsets, overlap lookup, and evidence spans.
- It never calls `GraphHsmm`, never constructs an `AlignmentMatrix`, never computes a `RecallSignature`, and shows no library-derived plot. The only substantive image is the project mark; the remaining SVGs are Starlight controls.
- `npm run verify` checks Astro, the static build, and verbatim artifact copying. It does not compile the exact Scala snippets, derive the displayed outputs, or generate/check a plot.
- The landing Anna story is useful controlled-method exposition, but `AnnaFixture` lives under `align/src/test` and injects semantic distances. It is not an ordinary consumer artifact and must not silently stand in for the runnable public path.

A real public path already exists and I exercised it now from the current main source:

`WarOfTheGhostsModel.model -> StorySourceView.validated -> StorySource.fromText(raw recall) -> RecallSegmenter.segment -> SemanticDistance.lexicalJaccard -> CandidateGenerator.generate -> GraphHsmm.infer -> RecallSignature.compute`

This ran successfully in `fixturesJVM/Test/console` using only main-scope public APIs. Five published WOG paraphrases segmented into six recall units. Exact observed result with the free lexical-Jaccard channel:

- Viterbi: all six units were `External(Intrusion)`.
- uniform coverage: `0.011535667262520937`.
- fidelity: `0.5588`, supported by only `0.8331/0.8331` anchored mass.
- specificity: `0.3086`, with support `0.8331/6.0000`.
- discourse chronology: `0.4973`, but support only `0.0225/5.0000`.
- causal preservation: `n/a`, support `0.0000/9.0000`.
- external report: attributed `0.8611`, unranked `0.0000`, ranked `1.0000`.

This is not a showcase accuracy result; it is a valuable honest demonstration that the mechanics run while the free lexical baseline performs poorly on these paraphrases. The docs must not massage it into success. They should explain what each output means and why low support prevents broad interpretation.

Concrete docs correction:

1. Replace the main Scala quickstart job with this end-to-end public workflow. Keep the atlas material as a later task page titled around source evidence.
2. Compile or execute the exact published snippet and derive displayed output from that same run.
3. Plot the posterior as recall-unit rows against source anchors plus named external states. This makes uncertainty and outside mass visible.
4. Plot the Viterbi or transition path over story order, including backward moves and external excursions.
5. Render the signature as measures paired with support/missingness; `causal = n/a, support 0/9` is an essential result, not fine print.
6. Keep the controlled Anna example, but label its injected distances and test-only status. Use it to explain intended behavior, not claim ordinary consumer performance.
7. Give the big library a visible capability path: source evidence -> typed propositions -> story contexts/time/causality -> recall units -> candidate channels -> gated alignment -> signatures -> interview scoring -> codecs/output views.

The owner requirement is therefore still unmet in the current mutable successor. The needed material is present in public APIs and tests; the docs have so far stopped at the first layer.
